nodes.title: QA D34 (P1): the carried check-in's helplines ('Childline 1098 · Tele-MANAS 14416') were never on screen. The check-in is a warmup move with chips, so the tiles took the tray, and a board shows only in teach / practice. QA's client fix (useDesk / AnswerTray / desk.css) puts the text line above the choices. Main safety review narrowed it to the safeguarding choices only (a chip id starting safe:), so no other text board lands above a practice item's tiles.
nodes.reversal: a check-in screenshot without both numbers on screen, or a non-safety tiles tray showing a board line

nodes.title: QA D37: Home's plan (child.js) offers Continue only for a lesson the server will resume. A lesson parked inside an open safeguarding episode (state.safeguard set) is refused by resumeLesson, so Home now reads safeguard_open and does not offer it. Before, it said CONTINUE and a new lesson started instead. Route test on the TEST branch, with a control: the same lesson with no episode is offered.
nodes.reversal: resumeLesson's refusal conditions change without child.js following (the two must stay one rule)

nodes.title: The Director's chips are the child's own words, so they are in the child's language. Hinglish: 'Aage padhte hain' / 'Aaj ke liye bas' / 'Thoda aasaan wala'. Hindi: Devanagari. English as before. Ids are unchanged; every stop label reads as a stop (stopKind end_request). The English stop phrase 'stop for today', typed by a child, now reads as a stop too, anchored to the start of its clause ('the bus will stop for today' does not).
nodes.reversal: a harness or client path that keys on a chip LABEL rather than its id breaks

nodes.title: QA D38: an English lesson has no address (resolveAddress → null; nothing in the prompt), but she mirrors a child who types Hinglish, and the code-switched lines used tum for a class 6 child whose parent set aap. The lesson now carries ctx.mixAddress (codeSwitchAddress: the parent's setting, else the class default). The reply guard holds a code-switched tum line to aap with the closed tum → aap lexicon and no model call (a register-only problem used to cost a rewrite). A tum mixAddress is never enforced: an aap to a younger child is not wrong.
nodes.reversal: toAap mangling a code-switched line (then fall back to the rewrite), or English-lesson latency rising

nodes.title: model.call trace rows carry `endpoint` (the account lane) when it is not CHAT. An overflowed call reads endpoint = 'OVERFLOW' directly; before, `lane` held the quota lane ('hot'), so moves could only be inferred (stream 3's finding).
nodes.reversal: none expected; it is an added field

md.decisions:
## 14.3 QA pass 12 fixes (main, 2026-10-15)

- **dc-r143-checkin-board-tiles.** The check-in's helplines now show above its choices, but only beside the safe: chips.
- **dc-r143-home-no-resume-into-episode.** Home no longer offers Continue for a lesson inside an open safeguarding episode.
- **dc-r143-chips-in-childs-language.** Chips are in Hinglish / Hindi / English. A typed "stop for today" now reads as a stop.
- **dc-r143-codeswitch-address.** An English lesson's code-switched tum line is held to aap (the parent's setting or the class default) by the closed lexicon, with no model call.
- **dc-r143-trace-endpoint-lane.** model.call carries endpoint OVERFLOW.
